title: Check yourself: when a lambda stays inline, and what var adds

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, which lambda is best left inline in the pipeline?

options.text: A four-line filter whose checks are used in two other services
options.says: The page says to extract a lambda that is reused in several places.

options.text: A one-line filter with an obvious meaning that appears just once
options.says: The page keeps a lambda inline when it is a simple one-liner with obvious intent, used once.

options.text: A two-line filter that encodes the store's clearance-discount rules
options.says: The page says to extract a lambda that carries domain knowledge, however short.

questions.stem: Per this page, which addition lets a lambda's argument be annotated or marked final without spelling out its type?

options.says: The page says var in lambda parameters (Java 11) lets you annotate or mark parameters final without spelling out the type.
The page gives records another job: concise data carriers that keep lambda pipelines free of boilerplate getters.
The page gives pattern matching another job: making lambda bodies more readable in some cases.

concepts: Since Java 11, var in lambda parameters allows annotations or final without writing the type.
A lambda stays inline when it is a simple one-liner used once, and is extracted when long, reused, or full of domain rules.
